program.name: SGL-001 development program
program.current_formulation_hypothesis: Intranasal mesenchymal-stromal-cell-derived small-EV preparation with defined identity, purity, dose, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay; therapeutic cargo remains to be selected.
program.largest_unresolved_risk: Intranasal CNS exposure observed in rodents may not translate to larger species or humans.
program.next_proposed_action: Initiate the two-stage gate: (A) finalize source-cell, create MCB/WCB, define orthogonal QC panel and draft release specs, perform small-scale process dev; (B) run biodistribution/PK/PD bridging study in rodents and a large species (preferably NHP) with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls and prespecified acceptance criteria.

evidence.title: Treatment of brain inflammatory diseases by delivering exosome encapsulated anti-inflammatory drugs from the nasal region to the brain
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: in mouse models, intranasal exosomes carrying curcumin or a STAT3 inhibitor were reported to reach brain microglia and improve model-specific inflammatory or tumor outcomes. These findings are preclinical and formulation-specific.

metadata.model_or_indication: mouse brain inflammation and glioma models

evidence.title: Intranasal MSC-derived A1-exosomes ease inflammation, and prevent abnormal neurogenesis and memory dysfunction after status epilepticus
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: after status epilepticus in young mice, intranasally administered human MSC-derived EVs were reported in the hippocampus and were associated with reduced neuronal loss and inflammation and preservation of neurogenesis and cognitive or memory outcomes versus vehicle.

evidence.title: Extracellular vesicles from immortalized mesenchymal stromal cells protect against neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: repeated intranasal EV administration after hypoxic-ischemic injury reduced brain tissue atrophy in neonatal mice; EVs from a clonal immortalized MSC line and primary MSCs showed comparable effects. The study frames source-cell consistency and scale as translational considerations.

evidence.title: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV2023): From basic to advanced approaches
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: the ISEV consensus identifies continuing challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular particles, characterization, functional studies, production reporting, and in-vivo evaluation; it recommends transparent, orthogonal characterization and appropriate controls.

evidence.title: Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of extracellular vesicles administered intravenously and intranasally to Macaca nemestrina
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: reporter-labeled Expi293F-derived EVs administered intranasally to macaques were not reliably detected above background in CSF, showed negligible brain uptake, and were strongly retained in nasal lavage. EV source, formulation, labeling, administration, and species may affect generalizability.

claims.statement: Intranasally administered EV preparations have been reported to reach CNS compartments or CNS-resident cells in multiple mouse studies.
claims.rationale: The cited mouse studies reported brain or hippocampal localization after intranasal administration; this does not establish delivery in humans.

claims.statement: Rodent intranasal MSC-derived EVs show reproducible benefit in injury models and justify further candidate-defining and translational studies but do not by themselves demonstrate intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species.
claims.rationale: Multiple rodent studies show functional benefit; however, these data do not quantify intact-EV CNS exposure or cross-species translation.

claims.statement: An immortalized/clonal MSC source can reduce heterogeneity and is a plausible manufacturing route but is not sufficient without MCB/WCB, process validation, and lot-to-lot potency/stability data.
claims.rationale: Single-study activity from an immortalized line supports feasibility but lacks scale-up and GMP bridging data.

claims.statement: Minimum CMC must include a chosen source-cell with MCB/WCB plan, orthogonal EV identity/purity panel per MISEV, draft release specifications, stability-indicating assays, and a mechanism-linked potency assay to control biological activity across batches.
claims.rationale: MISEV2023 defines orthogonal characterization and reporting expectations that translate into minimum CMC elements, but product-specific limits and validated assays remain to be generated.

claims.statement: Intranasal CNS delivery of EVs does not reliably translate across species: one macaque study found negligible brain uptake and no reliable CSF signal after intranasal administration of Expi293F-derived EVs.
claims.rationale: This directly limits extrapolation from rodent localization studies; differences in EV source, formulation, labeling, dosing, and administration remain possible explanations.

hypothesis.statement: A two-stage gate (source-cell/CMC definition then rodent+large-animal biodistribution/PK/PD) will determine whether intranasal SGL-001 achieves reproducible intact‑EV CNS exposure and mechanism-relevant PD in a large species.
hypothesis.rationale: Bridging biodistribution and validated analytics are required to test cross-species translation and to tie in vitro potency concepts to in vivo PD.
hypothesis.test_plan: Stage 1: finalize source-cell, create MCB/WCB, define orthogonal QC panel and draft release specs, run small-scale process dev and stability assays. Stage 2: biodistribution/PK/PD in rodents and a bridging large species (preferably NHP) with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls; prespecified quantitative acceptance criteria for intact-EV CNS exposure, assay LLOQs/specificity, PK variability thresholds, and demonstration of mechanism-linked PD.

critique.summary: The hypothesis is plausible enough to test but remains highly sensitive to EV source, preparation purity, label artifacts, disease-model permeability, nasal retention, dose normalization, and cross-species anatomy. Rodent efficacy cannot establish that SGL-001 reaches a clinically relevant human CNS compartment or will benefit patients.
challenges: Demonstrate that measured CNS signal represents intact candidate-associated EV exposure rather than free label, co-isolates, or secondary biological effects.
Define product identity, purity, dose units, stability, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay before interpreting efficacy reproducibility.
Use a staged translational plan because the macaque biodistribution result conflicts with assuming that rodent intranasal brain uptake will generalize to humans.

risks.title: Cross-species uncertainty in intranasal intact-EV CNS delivery
risks.description: Rodent intranasal biodistribution may not predict quantitative CNS exposure in larger species; NHP data suggest lower/variable CNS exposure and risk of dominant non-vesicular label signal.
risks.mitigation: Require bridging biodistribution/PK/PD in a large species with validated intact-EV analytics and appropriate controls before advancement.

risks.title: CMC: identity, impurity control, and potency assay readiness
risks.description: Draft release specifications and potency concepts exist but lack validation, stability data, and lot-to-lot consistency across scaled runs.
risks.mitigation: Establish MCB/WCB, orthogonal QC per MISEV, develop and validate potency assay linked to in vivo PD, and run multiple scale-up batches to demonstrate reproducibility.

risks.title: Model generalizability from injury models to cognition/aging endpoints
risks.description: Efficacy evidence is from acute/injury rodent models; relevance to cognition/aging indications is unproven.
risks.mitigation: Defer indication-specific efficacy studies until biodistribution/PD linkage is demonstrated; design follow-on efficacy models that reflect intended clinical endpoints.

decision.question: Execute two-stage candidate-definition and biodistribution gate (source-cell/CMC definition then rodent+large-species biodistribution/PK/PD) before treating SGL-001 as candidate-like?
decision.rationale: Recommended to mitigate high translational risk from uncertain cross-species intranasal intact-EV delivery and to generate product-defining CMC and potency evidence needed for interpretable biodistribution and downstream efficacy studies.
